proof.criterion: A1 — ListenerPermissions publishes notifications.> in place of the stream prefixes, role lanes and exception lanes, with the rendered cloud-config goldens following (all three rendered users: example-host-a, example-dispatch, example-hub).
proof.surface: In-pod live rig: real nats-server v2.15.1 (the hub's version, go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@v2.15.1) started on the authorization this tree's own core.ListenerPermissions("example-hub")/core.SessionPermissions() render through core.Authorization.Render, with packages/envoy/cmd/listener built from this head running as that nkey user and a credential-free session (the server's no_auth_user) subscribed on notifications.lxspec.>. The grant is rendered by the branch's code, never typed by hand.
proof.command: go run ./rigtmp -listener /tmp/rig/listener-new (throwaway rig in packages/envoy/infra, deleted before completion): POST /v1/messages/publish {"topic":"notifications.lxspec.probe.all","message":"ad-hoc probe"}. Golden gate beside it: cd packages/envoy/infra && go test ./gcp/ -skip 'DataDisk'.
proof.observed: The rendered listener publish allow list is 41 entries headed by the single subject notifications.> (it was 50 entries of stream prefixes and lanes before). The publish answered 200 OK in 8ms and the subscribed session received 319 bytes on notifications.lxspec.probe.all; the nats-server log holds no violation. go test ./gcp/ -skip 'DataDisk' → ok (5.1 s), the cloud-config goldens matching.
proof.negativeControl: The same rig built in a copy of the base commit 2de87cd4f6fe, so the grant comes from the pre-change core.ListenerPermissions (50 publish entries: notifications.agent.>, …, notifications.role.>, notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.>), with the same new listener binary: the publish answered 500 Internal Server Error in 4ms with `bus: NATS denied the publish to "notifications.lxspec.probe.all": nats: permissions violation`, nats-server logged `Publish Violation - Subject "notifications.lxspec.probe.all"`, and the subscriber received nothing within 10 s.

proof.criterion: A2 — every notifications. topic the stream does not capture goes over core NATS with a server confirmation, so the publish is answered at once instead of waiting out JetStream's five-second acknowledgement.
proof.surface: The same in-pod rig, through the real listener binary and a real nats-server; the publish is timed from the HTTP request.
proof.command: go run ./rigtmp -listener /tmp/rig/listener-new: the timed POST /v1/messages/publish of notifications.lxspec.probe.all (and of notifications.lxspec.probe.control).
proof.observed: 200 OK in 8 ms for the first publish and 2 ms for the second, each delivered to the subscribing session (319 and 318 bytes).
proof.negativeControl: The same rig and the same (new) grant, but the listener binary built from the base commit 2de87cd4f6fe: the identical publish answered 500 Internal Server Error in 5.003s with {"error":"context deadline exceeded"} — the reported bug — while the core subscriber had already received the message.

proof.criterion: A3 — the listener refuses a topic outside notifications. with a 400, and its tests stay as the adopted pull request has them.
proof.surface: The same in-pod rig against the built listener.
proof.observed: 400 Bad Request in 2ms: {"error":"topic must begin with notifications.","expected":["topic"]}.
proof.negativeControl: On the same rig and in the same run, {"topic":"notifications.lxspec.probe.control"} answered 200 OK in 2ms and was delivered, so the 400 is the prefix rule and not a blanket refusal. Separately, the pre-change listener binary accepted outside.example into the publish path (no 400): it answered 500 after 5.002 s and nats-server logged `Publish Violation - Subject "outside.example"`.

callerCensus.scope: Every production caller of the listener's /v1/messages/publish and of the client's publish, re-taken on this branch's tree (the census behind the 400 was taken on main, which this branch is 208 commits behind).

callerCensus.finding: No production caller on this branch publishes outside notifications., and no test does either: every /v1/messages/publish topic in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api_test.go, main_test.go and startup_test.go is a notifications. topic. packages/envoy/internal/broker/wake/envoy.go deliberately uses /v1/messages/send instead, so the refusal does not reach it. Nothing had to be escalated to the architect.

simplifyPass.ran: skill://ce-simplify-code once at 7424e75ad6a16beadd5eef7d119d2936f40d0c4d, three reviewer personas (code-reuse, code-quality, efficiency) on the pull request's own diff
findings: Reuse subjectsOverlap in streamCaptures instead of the prefix/length test (P2, confidence 0.75) — skipped: it changes matching semantics for a wildcard subject in the publish path (behaviour preservation not established) and would diverge this branch's hunk from the main-line fix.

Collapse usesCoreTransport's two role-lane clauses into the new one (P3, all three reviewers) — skipped: the two clauses are the standing guarantee that a role lane never reaches JetStream, independent of what streamSubjects compiles in; thinning it is a safety check the skill forbids removing, and it would diverge from the main-line fix.

Precompute the trimmed stream-subject prefixes (P3) — skipped: an allocation-free scan of eight entries beside a JSON marshal and a network hop, and a divergence from the main-line fix for no measurable gain.

Drop TestAnAdHocPublishNATSDeniesReturnsTheDenial as a near-duplicate of TestPublishCoreReportsAPublishNATSDenies (P3, confidence 0.5) — skipped: the spec requires the adopted tests to stay as the pull request has them.
simplifyPass.verdict: 0 applied, so the head is unchanged and no re-proof was needed. All three reviewers reported the change behaviourally correct. Every finding belongs to the main line (dispatch://INFRA-113) if it is taken at all, because this branch's criterion is equivalence with that fix.

localGates: cd packages/envoy/infra && go test ./gcp/ -skip 'DataDisk' → ok (5.1 s), the cloud-config golden gate
cd packages/envoy/infra && go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./... → clean (compiles the live files without running them)

cd packages/envoy && go test ./cmd/listener/ ./internal/bus/ → not runnable in this pod: internal/testnats starts every server through testcontainers and the pod has no Docker. CI's envoy-go and envoy-infra-go are those suites' surface.
trickyParts: The adoption had to keep b096a8708's tree byte for byte. jj describe rewrites the duplicated commit, so the commit id printed by jj duplicate is stale afterwards: using it in jj new resurrected the obsolete copy and left the change id divergent. Fixed by jj new on the described commit and jj abandon on the stale one; the branch carries one commit, 7424e75a.

The adopted commit keeps its human author (sami@thecybermonk.com) by design, with the implement App as committer, so the identity check shows a human author on exactly that commit. The check is run with the base's revset, not the repository default branch's, or it lists the base's 290 commits.
Local Go commands wrote go.work.sum; that incidental change was restored (jj restore go.work.sum) so the pull request carries only the twelve files.
deviations: The plan's adoption check ("jj diff --from b096a8708 --to <adopted commit> --git prints nothing") was written for an adoption commit sitting directly on the base. Here it sits on the two plan commits, so the check was run with the '~.legion' fileset, which prints nothing; without the fileset the only difference is .legion/INFRA-117/plan.json.

The spec names permissions_live_test.go and dispatch_permissions_live_test.go as the live surface. They need Docker, which this pod has not, so the proof above is the plan's approved substitute (plan section 5, D4; the architect approved it on 2026-10-22): the same server, the same rendered grant and the same listener binary, driven by hand, plus CI's natslive step.
discoveredComplexity: The pre-change listener answers a publish to a topic outside notifications. the same way it answers an ad-hoc notification topic — 500 after 5 s — and nats-server logs a Publish Violation for outside.example even under the new grant, since notifications.> does not cover it. The new 400 is what turns that into an immediate, named refusal.

The dispatch CI job is failure at this head, in step 13 "Test dispatch dashboard" — the same job and the same step as the plan's baseline, #2089's merged head c00fcb28eab9a3b4831007e2cd0996ef1f044021, so it is pre-existing on this branch line and not this change's. It is not in the plan's by-hand job list (which names dispatch-memory, not dispatch).
